subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation LAN stand for?
options: Local Area Network
Large Access Node
Linked Address Network
Logical Area Node
questions.explain: A LAN (Local Area Network) connects devices over a small geographical area such as a single site or building.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the difference between a LAN and a WAN?
options: A WAN covers a large geographical area and usually uses infrastructure owned by third parties, while a LAN covers a small area on one site
A LAN always uses fibre optic cable, while a WAN always uses copper
A WAN can only connect two computers, while a LAN connects many
A LAN is wireless, while a WAN is always wired
questions.explain: A WAN spans a wide area and typically relies on third-party infrastructure, whereas a LAN is confined to a single site.

questions.q: In a star topology, how are the devices connected?
options: Each device connects to a central switch or hub
Each device connects directly to every other device
Devices are connected in a single closed loop
Devices share one common backbone cable
questions.explain: In a star topology every node has its own connection to a central switch or hub.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of a mesh topology over a star topology?
options: There is no single point of failure because data can take multiple routes
It requires the fewest cables and is cheapest to install
All traffic must pass through one central device
It cannot be used for wireless connections
questions.explain: In a mesh, nodes interconnect and data can be rerouted, so one failed link does not bring the network down.

questions.q: Which piece of hardware uses MAC addresses to forward data frames only to the intended device on a LAN?
options: Switch
Modem
Repeater
Router
questions.explain: A switch reads the MAC address of each frame and forwards it only to the port of the destination device.

questions.q: What is the main function of a router on a network?
options: To forward data packets between different networks
To convert digital signals to analogue for phone lines
To store shared files for all users
To boost a weak wireless signal only
questions.explain: A router directs data packets between networks, for example between a home LAN and the internet.

questions.q: Which is a characteristic of a client-server network rather than a peer-to-peer network?
options: Files and resources are managed centrally by a dedicated server
Every computer has equal status and stores its own files
There is no need for any central management software
It is only suitable for two or three home computers
questions.explain: In a client-server model a central server manages resources, security and file storage for the clients.

questions.q: A school network becomes very slow at lunchtime when many pupils stream video at once. Which factor is most directly causing this?
options: The available bandwidth is being shared among many users
The MAC addresses of the devices have changed
The IP addressing scheme has run out of protocols
The switch has stopped using packet switching
questions.explain: Bandwidth is finite and shared, so a high number of simultaneous users reduces the throughput available to each.

questions.q: In networking, what is a protocol?
options: A set of rules governing how devices communicate
A physical cable that joins two computers
A type of malware that spreads between devices
A unique number identifying a device on a network
questions.explain: A protocol is an agreed set of rules that allows devices to exchange data reliably.

questions.q: Which protocol is the secure version of HTTP that encrypts data sent between a browser and a web server?
options: HTTPS
FTP
SMTP
POP
questions.explain: HTTPS adds encryption (via TLS/SSL) to HTTP so that web traffic cannot easily be read if intercepted.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to send email from a client to a mail server?
options: SMTP
IMAP
POP3
HTTP
questions.explain: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send outgoing email, while IMAP and POP3 retrieve it.

questions.q: What is the main role of TCP in the TCP/IP protocol suite?
options: Breaking data into packets and reassembling them reliably at the destination
Assigning a unique address to identify each device
Encrypting all web traffic automatically
Physically transmitting signals along the cable
questions.explain: TCP splits data into numbered packets, checks for errors and reassembles them in the correct order at the receiver.

questions.q: What is the main role of IP in the TCP/IP protocol suite?
options: Addressing packets and routing them across networks
Reassembling packets into the correct order
Retrieving email from a mail server
Compressing files before transfer
questions.explain: IP (Internet Protocol) handles the addressing and routing of packets so they reach the correct destination network.

questions.q: The TCP/IP model organises protocols into how many layers?
options: Four
Two
Seven
Ten
questions.explain: The TCP/IP model has four layers: application, transport, internet and network access (link).

questions.q: Why is the TCP/IP stack divided into separate layers?
options: Each layer can be developed and changed independently without affecting the others
It makes data travel physically faster along the cable
It removes the need for any protocols
It stops packets from ever being lost
questions.explain: Layering makes the system modular, so a protocol in one layer can be updated without redesigning the others.

questions.q: A user wants to upload several large files to a remote web server for storage. Which protocol is designed for transferring files like this?
options: FTP
SMTP
HTTPS
IMAP
questions.explain: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is specifically designed for transferring files between a client and a server.

questions.q: Which term describes software written specifically to damage or gain unauthorised access to a computer system?
options: Malware
Firmware
Firewall
Freeware
questions.explain: Malware is malicious software, including viruses, worms, trojans and ransomware, designed to harm or exploit systems.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a phishing attack?
options: Sending fake messages that trick users into revealing personal or login details
Flooding a server with requests so it cannot respond
Guessing passwords by trying many combinations automatically
Inserting malicious SQL into a database input field
questions.explain: Phishing uses deceptive emails or messages that impersonate trusted sources to steal confidential information.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a firewall on a network?
options: To monitor and control incoming and outgoing traffic based on rules
To encrypt all files stored on the hard drive
To back up data automatically to the cloud
To increase the network bandwidth
questions.explain: A firewall inspects network traffic and blocks or permits it according to a set of security rules.

questions.q: A company wants to ensure that even if data is intercepted while being transmitted, it cannot be read by the attacker. Which measure should they use?
options: Encryption
A stronger topology
Increasing the bandwidth
Adding more switches
questions.explain: Encryption scrambles data so that intercepted information is unreadable without the correct decryption key.
